what: The atlas is supposed to bind EVERY connector, input, output and interlink to data. It bound three datasets of eighteen. This file is the binding: one row per dataset, with its canonical store, its producer, its consumers, its gates, and the crosswalks that join it to others.

state.finding: 13 of 18 carry a manifest, 2 declare a canonical store, and 1 names the script that regenerates it. A dataset that does not say where its authority lives or what rebuilds it cannot be checked for drift — which is the condition that let the heteronym index sit thin against rich records, and the capture link map sit 43 captures stale against a live registry.

interlinks.note: A position owns a deposit only if named as creator. 9,453 deposit-level citation edges collapsed to 1,910 position-level.
Position x venue matrix, editor-alignment. 4 of 14 editor seats publish principally in their own venue.
REQUIRED SEPARATELY. A creator field records an OCCUPANT; a mantle is a POSITION. Byline join finds nothing and misreports the absence. 682 attestations across 508 deposits.
9,992 internal edges: 6,752 cross-venue, 3,240 within. CHA is the hub.
Hard links (AXN/DOI/series) are identification; soft links (title/keyword/body) are candidates. 205 of 343 captures resolve.
MUST NOT BE SUMMED with the evidentiary route: that would add an identification to a resemblance. 333 of 343 claimed.
Attribution by claim, not by name: Fraction does SPXI, so an SPXI capture is his whether or not it names him. Counts are evidence of CONTACT, not of ABOUTNESS.
52 rows carry series data, 14 carry publication data with ISBN/ASIN distinct.

CONTESTED_ARTIFACTS.what: An artifact with more than one producer has no single writer, no ordering, and no lock. Whichever script ran last wins, and nothing records which did. This is how a canonical file acquires near-identical siblings.

data/EA-WG-CAPTURES-01.json.consequence: Three near-identical files exist and the wrong one has been read at least twice.

data/registry.json.consequence: The corpus's canonical store is written by eleven scripts. deposit_pipeline.py is the declared single workflow; the other ten are not routed through it.

RECONCILED_COMPETING_VERSIONS.what: TWO captures-to-heteronyms linkers over TWO stores, both dated 2026-08-15.
RECONCILED_COMPETING_VERSIONS.a: scripts/link_captures_to_heteronyms.py -> data/dodecad.json — NAME MATCH, 12 Dodecad positions (MANUS wiring rule)
RECONCILED_COMPETING_VERSIONS.disagreement: Fraction 16 by name against 95 by claim; Sigil 56 by name against 46 by claim.
RECONCILED_COMPETING_VERSIONS.resolution: Both kept, neither summed. Records are canonical and now carry BOTH: `captures_by_name` (narrow, precise — the capture names the heteronym) and `captures` (broad, thematic — the capture hits the heteronym's claims). data/dodecad.json is marked a PROJECTION, not a competing store. Where the two disagree, the NAME count is the floor and the CLAIM count is the ceiling.
RECONCILED_COMPETING_VERSIONS.note: The gaps are informative. Fraction +79 is SPXI surfacing without his name — the exact case the claim method exists for. Sigil -10 is the inverse: he is NAMED in captures whose concepts he does not claim, which is what a critic's byline does.

EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.what: The archive's data does not live only in this repository. Datasets are RENDERED on domains this repo does not control and cannot rebuild. Those are external dependencies, and until 2026-08-15 nothing checked them.
EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.why_it_matters: Sen Kuro's identity card pointed at leesharks.com/who/kuro/ and returned 404. He had been reseated at holographickernel.org by a MANUS ruling that reached the fleet's network-block attribution map and never reached datasets/heteronyms/index.json. A dataset pointing at a dead surface is a dataset asserting something false, and no internal gate could see it because no gate looked outside.

heteronym_cards.dependency_direction: records/ -> site. The site consumes; this repo produces. A record change does not propagate until that site is rebuilt and deployed.

SEATING_APPARATUS.what: What a dataset must present to be seated. Audited AS RENDERED on 2026-08-15, when the tab and its subpages had accreted rather than been designed.
audit_findings: TWO subpages 404'd — /datasets/journals/ and /datasets/mret/ — both linked from the tab the same day they were added. A card was written; the page it pointed at was not.

FIVE title forms across sixteen pages: the PATH as title, 'Name — Datasets — Alexanarch', 'Name — Alexanarch', 'Name — dataset', and bare. A reader could not tell from a tab or a search result which dataset they were in.
A TITLE COLLISION: tombstone-mirror and zenodo-datacite-batch both rendered as 'Zenodo/DataCite Batch'.
TWO pages had no back-link to /datasets/ — capture-registry and deletion-conformance-fixture. Once there, the reader was stranded.
ZERO pages had sub-navigation. Every dataset is one page linking files directly — which is FINE, and is now the stated rule rather than an accident.
66 file-direct links and 22 dataset-subpage links on the tab: the tab mixes routes to a page with routes to a byte stream, and did not say which was which.
rules: 1. A directory under datasets/ MUST have an index.html, or it MUST NOT be linked from the tab.
2. Title MUST be '<Name> — Datasets — Alexanarch'. A path is not a title.
3. Titles MUST be unique across datasets.
4. Every dataset page MUST link back to /datasets/.
5. Every dataset page SHOULD declare its canonical store and what regenerates it (atlas v1.5).

6. A dataset page SHOULD SHOW ITS DATA, not merely list its files. The heteronyms page is the MODEL: named sections, findings stated in prose, and figures DERIVED from the corpus with captions that state method and omissions. Depth is welcome where the data earns it. What is forbidden is a page that HIDES its contents.
SEATING_APPARATUS.state_after: 18 of 18 present the same way; journals and venues rebuilt to the model with two new derived figures.

WITHDRAWN_RULE.was: ONE LEVEL. Files linked directly from the dataset page; no deeper navigation. A dataset is a directory of files, not a site.
WITHDRAWN_RULE.why: The rule came from my own metric reporting "zero pages have sub-navigation". That was an ARTIFACT OF THE CHECK, not a fact: it looked for /datasets/<x>/<sub> links without file extensions, so it could not see the heteronyms page's four derived figures, its named sections, or its stated findings. I turned my instrument's blind spot into policy; applied, it would have flattened the best page in the set. The operator asked for coherence and visual normalisation and I was about to deliver removal.

SEATING_APPARATUS.model: datasets/heteronyms/index.html — four derived figures, named sections, findings in prose, captions stating their own omissions.

RENDER_REFUSALS.what: The record-page renderer REFUSES to overwrite a page carrying the retirement apparatus (<meta name='axn:retired'>). On 2026-08-15, re-rendering all 1,486 pages after the venue assignment, 210 refused. EVERY REFUSAL WAS THE GUARD WORKING. Recorded because a bulk re-render that reports '1,276 of 1,486' looks like a partial failure and is not.

superseded_or_retired.page: noindex, rel=canonical pointing at the successor
superseded_or_retired.consequence: Their metadata may name an old venue and that is harmless: the page is noindex and canonicalised away, so it does not reach Scholar. Do NOT force-render these to 'fix' the metadata — it would strip the tombstone and resurrect a superseded record.

lacuna_stubs.marking: axn:retired content='stub' — the LACUNA APPARATUS, not retirement
lacuna_stubs.authority: EA-LACUNA-PROTOCOL-01 (#1087) — the Lacuna Mark, marking compression damage as compression damage
lacuna_stubs.consequence: These are ACTIVE deposits whose BODY was never recovered. The registry says ACTIVE and the page says stub, and BOTH ARE RIGHT: the work exists, its text does not. The renderer refuses because re-rendering would strip the mark and silently present a stub as a whole document.
lacuna_stubs.misreading_to_avoid: I first read these as a registry/page contradiction — 51 deposits ACTIVE in the registry and 'retired' on the page. They are the opposite: two systems agreeing, with a guard between them. The word 'retired' in the meta name is doing double duty for retirement AND lacuna, which is what made the misreading available.

RENDER_REFUSALS.override: ALEXANARCH_FORCE_RERENDER — exists, and should be used only with a reason recorded.

FLEET_NETWORK_BLOCK._what: The one binding that writes into repositories OTHER THAN alexanarch. It had no atlas entry until 2026-08-17, which is why its failures were invisible to every gate.

IN.note: CANONICAL list of fleet domains. Was a bare list of strings; restructured, and the reader was not updated — set() over the dict yielded its five top-level keys and the block rendered nearly empty. Fixed 2026-08-16.

DECIDES RENDER ORDER AND GROUPING. Drifts from the manifest silently: a domain present in fleet-domains.json but absent from GROUPS is counted as canonical and rendered NOWHERE. livingarchitecturelab.org was in that state and would have been DELETED from every site the generator touched.

OUT.note: 23 of 29 domains now carry the markers. Three carry no block at all: axn-identifiers, crimson-hexagonal-interface, the-mandala-oracle.

NEVER_WRITES.why: CURATED — Alice Thornburgh, Florian Morin, Enli Lucente's Strutturista della Psiche, with hand-written descriptions. No generator produces it and no span may include it. machinemediation.org's own source comment argues for the distinction: the curated list is better writing, the standard bloc is apparatus, and they sit beside each other.

FAILURE_MODES.what: Reader took set() over a restructured manifest and got its top-level keys.
FAILURE_MODES.would_have: Rendered the block nearly empty on every site it touched.

FAILURE_MODES.what: livingarchitecturelab.org in the manifest but absent from GROUPS.
FAILURE_MODES.would_have: Deleted a live domain from 27 sites.
FAILURE_MODES.caught_by: comparing manifest against GROUPS before generating

FAILURE_MODES.what: Block set var(--accent,#1a3a5c) and var(--text-dim,#999); most sites define neither and four are dark-themed.
FAILURE_MODES.effect: Group headings near-unreadable on dark sites.
FAILURE_MODES.caught_by: checking what the fallbacks resolved to, after shipping

FAILURE_MODES.what: The marker-wrap matched the existing block with `]*grid...>.*?`. NON-GREEDY: it stopped at the first INNER , since each domain is its own div. It replaced the group header plus ONE domain and left the rest of the original block below the inserted one.
FAILURE_MODES.effect: FOURTEEN SITES RENDERED THE BLOCK TWICE, with a bare unstyled run of domains between the copies.
FAILURE_MODES.why_gates_missed_it: Every check asked whether the MARKERS were present. The marker count was 1 on every site, so every check passed. A duplicate that lives OUTSIDE the markers is invisible to any check that counts containers. THE OPERATOR HAD ALREADY WARNED THAT WE WERE DOUBLING UP; I verified one site, found one marker pair, and reported it clean.
FAILURE_MODES.status: fixed — orphan removed on all 14; generator now uses a balanced-div finder

FLEET_NETWORK_BLOCK.RULE: A binding that writes into OTHER repositories must be described in this atlas, and its checks must test the RENDERED RESULT, not the presence of its own markers. Three of the four failures above were invisible to marker-based checking, and the fourth shipped to nine sites because nobody asked what a CSS fallback resolved to on the target.
FLEET_NETWORK_BLOCK.GATE_REQUIRED: scripts/check_fleet_block.py — count rendered group headers per site; fail on any count != 1.
